brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A green tea from Huangzhu village on the outskirts of Yongxing County, Hunan.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It is described as a historical tea of the village, picked in spring. Little more is reliably documented about it.
processing: Picked, then fixed, rolled and pan-fired, with the rolling treated as the critical step.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Flat leaves thickly covered in white down, with some yellow to golden buds.
appearance_liquor: Pale yellow to light gold, clear and bright.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Mellow and sweet with a lasting returning sweetness and an aroma of flowers and light fruit.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
